reason: The attractions need a motor, and this is the only offered action.
expectation: I expect to mount the motor on the whale, though the separate drives will probably still need fitting.

effect: The motor is mounted; the attractions still need connections to it.
reaction: No particular surprise; that was the expected first fitting.
reason: The coupler is the only offered combination and should connect a crank to the motor.
expectation: I expect it to connect the motor to the dragon's crank, though the other attraction may need a separate drive.

effect: The dragon is now motor-driven; the star theatre still needs its drive.
reason: The belt drive is the only offered combination and should provide the other speed needed.
expectation: I expect the belt drive to connect the star theatre at a reduced speed, though it may still need a cover and switch.

effect: The belt drive gives the star wheel a slower speed than the dragon, using different pulley sizes.
reaction: The pulley explanation makes the different speeds easy to understand.
reason: The cover is the only offered combination and should guard the moving drive.
expectation: I expect the clear cover to protect the belt and pulleys while leaving them visible; the switch may still need fitting.

effect: The drive is now guarded; it still needs the master switch.
reaction: The cover was a predictable safety fitting.
reason: The switch is the only offered combination and should let us control the attractions together.
expectation: I expect it to connect the accessory power so the dragon and star wheel can be switched on and off.

effect: The switch runs both attractions, and the slipping clutch adds protection if the dragon is held still. The chapter goal is complete.
reaction: Seeing the two different motions work together is satisfying; the clutch was a useful surprise.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the reducing belt was most worthwhile: the different pulley sizes clearly explain why the stars move more slowly than the dragon.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mounting the motor was straightforward but offered little to think about on its own.

surprise.text: The clutch slipping when the dragon is held still was an unexpected protective detail.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although each decision had only one combination offered.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the connected attractions and the pending lifting test make me curious to see the fair operate as a whole, though the single-option sequence made the decisions predictable.
